title.narrative: Emergency WASH Support for Vulnerable Area C Communities in Southern West Bank

description.narrative: ltpgtCommunities in Area C of the southern West Bank—particularly in Masafer Yatta, East Yatta, East Bethlehem, Bani Neim, and along the Road 317—face continuing water insecurity due to settler violence targeting water pipelines, cisterns, and wells, compounded by systematic reductions in water allocations from Mekorot. According to OCHA, settler incidents have escalated sharply since early 2023, rising from an average of 1–2 incidents per month to nearly 5–6 per month in 2025. These attacks have severely impacted water infrastructure, resulting in well damage, pipeline damage, and property destruction. Combined restrictions and violence have left many communities dependent on costly private water trucking. lt/pgtltpgtThe proposed intervention will address these critical gaps by providing ltbgt4244 m³lt/bgt of emergency water trucking over around two months to vulnerable communities in Bani Neim specifically (Um Al Thahab and Zaatoot), Road 317 communities (Susiya , Ghzewi, Wad Jheish, Um Neer, Um Qussa, A Seefer and Saadet Tha`lab ), and East Yatta (Dkaika, Huwwara, Barouq and Khallet Hajar Fauqa Tahta ) meeting minimum WASH Cluster standards in West Bank (30 l/c/d) benefitting 429 HHs (2,145 individuals).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn addition, the project will rehabilitate ltbgt20 family-owned wells (cisterns)lt/bgt in East Yatta (Birin, Barouq, Khallet Ameera, and Ghzewi), directly benefiting ltbgt40 HHs (200 individuals)lt/bgt by restoring water storage capacity and reducing reliance on trucking. Beneficiary households will be selected based on vulnerability and technical feasibility criteria. lt/pgtltpgtltbgtltbrgtlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtTo strengthen household resilience, ltbgt274 portable water bladders (10 m³) for the benefit of 274 HHslt/bgt (1,370 individuals) will be distributed in Masafer Yatta specifically (Isfey Atihta, Isfey Al Fauqa, Khirbet al fakheit, Khirbet at Tabban, Mirkez, Halaweh, Jinba, Khirbet al Majaz), and in East Bethlehem specifically (Kisan, Minya, Tuqu), and in Road 317 communities specifically (Um neer, Huwwara, Barouq, Mantiqat Sahibal Butum, Qawawis, Susiya, A Seefer) providing discreet storage that minimizes the risk of confiscation and allows relocation in case of forced displacement.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtOverall, the intervention will reach approximately ltbgt642 households (around 3,210 individuals)lt/bgt without duplication, as some beneficiaries will benefit from multiple interventions. The project will ensure access to safe water, restore critical infrastructure, and enhance secure storage. This action aligns with the WASH Cluster’s strategic objectives to address WASH service disruptions caused by settler and military attacks or isolation, through the provision of emergency water trucking and WASH services. It also contributes to the 2025 Flash Appeal priorities for the West Bank, particularly by improving access to WASH services for vulnerable communities in Area Clt/pgtltpgtIn addition to these interventions, hygiene promotion and multi-thematic training sessions will be provided, focusing on women. These sessions will cover hygiene practices, safeguarding, child protection, and PSEAH. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will be implemented in coordination with WASH Cluster, PWA and local councils to deliver timely, life-saving water support to some of the most water-insecure and affected communities in the south of West Bank. MA’AN has coordinated with West Bank Protection Consortium members active in these areas, specifically Area C, to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication of interventions. MA’AN adheres to Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Child Protection, Anti-Fraud, Gender Inclusion, Code of Conduct, and Core Humanitarian Standards (CHS). A Complaints Response Mechanism (CRM) accessible to both beneficiaries and non-beneficiaries ensures accountability and facilitates feedbacklt/pgt
